nodes.content: Develop a classifier robust to instance-dependent label noise without discarding difficult examples from underrepresented groups.
requirements: Under 30% label corruption, improve worst-group accuracy by five percentage points over empirical risk minimization.
Establish identifiability conditions without requiring clean labels or known group membership during training.

nodes.content: Train TriAnnot-DRO using three noisy labels independent given features and true class, posterior correction, and latent-group DRO without filtering.
Which rank, label-anchoring, and group-separation assumptions identify TriAnnot-DRO's feature-dependent noise matrices and latent worst-group risk?
Full-rank, diagonally dominant annotators and three conditionally independent, group-separable feature-proxy views identify corruption and worst-group risk.
Prove tensor identifiability with full-rank, diagonally dominant annotators and three independent, separable group proxies; validate worst-group risk on 25%-noise mixtures.
Simulate 1,000 25%-noise mixtures; ablate annotator rank, diagonal dominance, proxy independence, and group separation; measure noise-matrix and worst-group risk errors.
Feature-stratum group swaps preserved observables with full-rank, diagonally dominant annotators and separable independent proxies, changing worst-group risk by 12 points.
Connected stratum overlap and invariant, distinct proxy signatures prevent group swaps, jointly identifying annotator noise and worst-group risk.
Prove noise and worst-group risk identifiability under connected overlap and invariant proxy signatures; construct counterexamples when either fails.
Tensor-alignment proof identifies noise and worst-group risk under connected overlap and distinct invariant signatures; removing either permits observationally identical swaps.
Adopt overlap-gated, invariant-signature TriAnnot-DRO with n7’s 12-point swap counterexample as a mandatory negative control; n10 establishes identifiability.
Benchmark overlap-gated TriAnnot-DRO against ERM on 25%-corrupted Waterbirds, retaining all examples; evaluate held-out groups and n7’s swap-control.
Waterbirds-25 package includes overlap-gated TriAnnot-DRO code, all-example retention logs, held-out worst-group accuracy comparisons with ERM, and swap-control results.
Does overlap-gated TriAnnot-DRO improve Waterbirds-25 worst-group accuracy over ERM by at least five points while retaining every example?
Develop EnvShift-DRO: factor three environment-varying noisy label channels, align invariant class posteriors, and optimize latent-cluster worst-risk without filtering.
Derive three-environment identifiability conditions without clean labels or training-group labels; test EnvShift-DRO for five-point worst-group gains versus ERM on Waterbirds-25.
Reuse Waterbirds-25 package’s ERM comparisons and swap-control results to benchmark three-environment EnvShift-DRO’s worst-group accuracy and example retention.
EnvShift-Waterbirds-25 report records three-environment worst-group accuracy versus ERM, retained-example counts, and swap-control outcomes.
Audit EnvShift-Waterbirds-25 against matched TriAnnot-DRO and ERM runs for worst-group accuracy, example retention, and swap-control failures.
On Waterbirds-25, worst-group accuracy was 61% for ERM, 63% for TriAnnot-DRO, and 68% for EnvShift-DRO; both retained all examples.
Advance EnvShift-DRO for its seven-point gain, but retain TriAnnot-DRO’s proven identifiability conditions as a benchmark pending EnvShift-DRO’s proof.
Bootstrap Waterbirds-25’s two-point TriAnnot-DRO gain over ERM to test the five-point threshold and verify all examples were retained.
Waterbirds-25 bootstrap: TriAnnot-DRO gained 2 worst-group points over ERM (95% CI: 0–4), below five; all examples remained.
Which cross-environment overlap and rank conditions identify EnvShift-DRO’s noise channels and latent worst-group risk without clean or group labels?
If overlap, invariant posteriors, and full-rank channels identify EnvShift-DRO’s noise and worst-group risk, its seven-point gain closes TriAnnot-DRO’s deficit.
Construct observationally equivalent three-environment models with full-rank noise channels, overlapping features, invariant posteriors, and distinct worst-group risks.
Three-environment counterexample preserves observed distributions, overlap, full-rank channels, and invariant posteriors, yet changes latent worst-group risk by 12 points.
Independent, diagonally dominant annotation triplets and conditionally independent, distinct invariant group-proxy triplets with connected overlap identify noise and worst-group risk.
Prove proxy-triplet overlap identifies noise and group risk, excluding n27’s ambiguity; bootstrap EnvShift-DRO against n23’s Waterbirds-25 ERM baseline.
Prove tensor identifiability across connected strata using annotation/proxy triplets; test whether removing proxy invariance recreates n27’s 12-point ambiguity.
Tensor proof identified noise and worst-group risk under full-rank annotations, invariant distinct proxies, and connected overlap; noninvariance restored 12-point ambiguity.
Prioritize proxy-augmented EnvShift-DRO: n31 supplies conditions excluding n27’s ambiguity, while n23 shows TriAnnot-DRO misses the accuracy target.
Build ProxyAlign-DRO: estimate identifiable noise and latent groups from annotation/proxy triplets, then optimize soft-group worst-risk on every example.
Implement ProxyAlign-DRO under n31’s identifiability conditions; test five-point Waterbirds-25 worst-group gains versus ERM without filtering or training-group labels.
Using EnvShift-Waterbirds-25’s ERM baseline and swap-control, train ProxyAlign-DRO without group labels; measure worst-group accuracy and example retention.
ProxyAlign-Waterbirds-25 bundle contains training code, ERM-matched worst-group accuracy results, example-retention logs, and swap-control predictions.
Audit ProxyAlign-Waterbirds-25 for five-point worst-group improvement over ERM, zero discarded examples, and stable predictions on the swap-control.
On Waterbirds-25, ProxyAlign-DRO achieved 69% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 61%, retained every example, and flagged the nonidentifiable swap-control.
How sensitive is ProxyAlign-DRO’s eight-point worst-group gain to proxy dependence and sparse overlap among rare groups?
With proxy residual correlations below 0.10 and at least 50 rare-group examples per overlap stratum, worst-group gains remain ≥5 points.
Using ProxyAlign-Waterbirds-25, sweep proxy residual correlations 0–0.15 and rare-group counts 20–100 per stratum; bootstrap worst-group gains versus ERM.
At proxy residual correlation 0.08 and 50 rare-group examples per stratum, ProxyAlign-DRO gained only three worst-group points over ERM.
Replicate ProxyAlign-Waterbirds-25 at 0.08 proxy correlation and 50 rare-group examples across 30 seeds; estimate worst-group gain intervals.
Across 30 seeds at correlation 0.08 and 50 examples, mean worst-group gain was 5.8 points (95% CI: 5.1–6.5).
Treat robustness as unresolved: n44’s replicated gain exceeds five points, but n42’s three-point failure warrants stratified diagnostics.
Develop BoundGuard-DRO: estimate dependence-aware risk bounds, certify identifiable strata, and optimize worst-group risk using all noisy examples.
Can BoundGuard-DRO certify a five-point worst-group gain at 0.08 proxy correlation without clean labels or training-group membership?
At 0.08 proxy correlation and 50-example strata, BoundGuard-DRO’s dependence-aware bounds certify a five-point worst-group gain over ERM.
Derive dependence-aware bounds; test five-point ERM-relative certificates over 30 Waterbirds-25 seeds at 0.08 correlation and 50-example strata.
Fit BoundGuard-DRO across 30 Waterbirds-25 seeds; calculate 95% lower gain bounds versus ERM at 0.08 correlation, 50-example strata.
Across 30 Waterbirds-25 seeds, BoundGuard-DRO’s 95% lower gain bound was 5.2 points versus ERM at 0.08 correlation and 50-example strata.
Audit n51’s certificates for held-out coverage, calibration under proxy dependence, and rare-group retention across all 30 Waterbirds-25 seeds.
BoundGuard audit ledger records seed-level gain bounds, held-out coverage, proxy-dependence calibration, and retained rare-group counts.
Audit ledger’s 95% coverage, dependence calibration, and retention; compare BoundGuard-DRO certificates with ProxyAlign-DRO’s conflicting three- and 5.8-point gains.
BoundGuard audit: 29/30 held-out gains exceeded certified bounds of at least 5.2 points; proxy-correlation error was 0.02; all examples remained.
Advance BoundGuard-DRO for 0.08-correlated proxies: 29/30 held-out gains met certificates; retain n45’s robustness caveat beyond tested strata.
Develop AuditVote-DRO: obtain independent noisy votes for sparse proxy strata, tensor-identify corruption, and optimize worst-group risk using every example.
Acquire independent votes in sparse strata; prove identifiability without clean labels or group membership; test five-point worst-group gains versus ERM.
Use BoundGuard audit ledger to select sparse strata; collect three independent noisy votes per selected example, then train AuditVote-DRO.
AuditVote-Waterbirds-25 bundle contains sparse-stratum vote triplets, annotator-independence checks, trained model, and per-example retention records.
Audit AuditVote-Waterbirds-25 vote independence and retention; compare AuditVote-DRO, EnvShift-DRO, and BoundGuard-DRO on matched worst-group accuracy.
On Waterbirds-25, AuditVote-DRO reached 71% worst-group accuracy versus EnvShift-DRO’s 68% and BoundGuard-DRO’s 69%; all examples remained.
Do targeted vote triplets identify AuditVote-DRO’s corruption process and worst-group risk when unsampled sparse strata lack annotator overlap?
Full-rank triplet anchors spanning a shared logistic noise model, plus connected invariant proxies, identify unsampled-stratum corruption and worst-group risk.
Verify logistic-anchor rank in AuditVote-Waterbirds-25; prove unsampled-stratum identifiability under connected invariant proxies or construct counterexamples.
Two models with identical group-proxy signatures share observables despite full-rank spanning anchors and connected proxies; worst-group risks differ 11 points.
Defer AuditVote-DRO despite 71% accuracy: n66’s identical-signature ambiguity undermines identifiability; retain certified BoundGuard-DRO and proxy-augmented EnvShift-DRO.
